title: Test doubles with Mockito and integration tests with Testcontainers

videos.script: OrderService places an order. It locks a row in PostgreSQL, takes the stock and saves the order through Spring Data. {{service}} Testing that against a real database is slow. And it tests the database as much as the service. {{slow}} So the first half of this lesson replaces the two repositories with mocks. Mockito builds them. You tell them what to answer, and afterwards you ask them what happened. {{mocks}} On the way the JDK complains about how Mockito gets into the test, and you fix that in the pom. {{agent}} Mocks have a blind spot. A mock repository never runs a query, so it can never find a wrong one. {{blind}} The second half runs the real thing. You install Docker Engine, and Testcontainers starts a fresh PostgreSQL for each test run. Flyway builds the schema, the tests run, and the container is gone. {{containers}} Maven keeps the two kinds apart. Surefire runs the fast tests, failsafe the slow ones. {{plugins}} And at the end you measure what the slow ones cost, in seconds. {{cost}}
